To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

lossy compression is superior to lossless compression, that lossy compression can be made arbitrarily close to lossless, that lossy text compression can achieve compression factors that are comparable to those of lossy image compression, and that the subjective quality of lossy text compression, when evaluated using the appropriate measures, is comparable to that of lossy image coding.

lossy text compression yields compression factors that are superior to those of lossless text compression, and that the resulting tradeoff curve between compression factor and perceived quality can be modeled using a combination of semantic and generative models.
lossy compression of text is a viable alternative to lossless compression, and that the quality of the compressed text can be quantified in terms of semantic and generative models.
